title: flagstaff plugin
description: A plugin is one plain object. Everything in it is data that can be read without running it; the only functions allowed are a component's `static` (required) and `frame` (optional). A spinner or component without a static projection is refused at register().

name.description: The plugin's name; also the prefix a host may use when two plugins contribute the same key.

contract.description: The plugin contract this object follows. A host refuses a newer contract than it knows.

tokens.description: A roundel theme: semantic token name to a hex colour, contrast-checked when flown.

glyphs.description: Symbols by meaning: `ok`, `fail`, `warn`, `info`, `running`. A plugin that ships glyphs changes every built-in that draws one.

spinners.description: Spinner styles by name, in cli-spinners' shape plus the static projection.

borders.description: Border styles a box can be drawn with, by name.

components.description: Components by name: `static(state)` returns the text a pipe, an agent or a screen reader gets; `frame(t, state)` is the optional animated form.

interval.description: Milliseconds between frames on a terminal.

static.description: What a pipe prints instead of the animation.
(state) => string. Required: the projection every non-terminal mode prints.

frame.description: (t, state) => string. Optional: the frame at t milliseconds since hoisting.

sample.description: Two states to *show* this component with: `flagstaff check` and the docs gallery render `running` then `done`. Omitted, they assume `{ phase: 'running' }` and `{ phase: 'done' }` and say so in the output. The loop never reads it — a running program's state comes from the program.

interval.description: Milliseconds between repaints when `frame` is given; 80 when omitted.

border.description: cli-boxes' shape exactly, so that corpus imports unchanged.

capability.description: One paratext capability: what it says to the terminal, when the terminal is believed to understand it, and what prints when it does not. No functions, so it travels through JSON. `encode` and `fallback` are templates: `{field}` is the field's value, `{field|base64}` is it base64-encoded, and `[ … ]` is emitted only when every field inside it has a value.

name.description: How callers name it. Registering an existing name replaces it — how a caller corrects a guess we got wrong.

osc.description: The OSC code this speaks, or 'BEL' for the bell and for protocols that are not OSC at all, such as Kitty's.

when.description: When the terminal is believed to understand it. Every clause must hold; `termProgram` and `envAny` are ORs within themselves. Guesses — no terminal answers 'do you do OSC 1337' — and therefore data a caller can replace.

tty.description: Refuse a pipe. Almost always true: a file that receives OSC gets control bytes in it.

termProgram.description: Any one of these TERM_PROGRAM values.

envAny.description: Any one of these environment variables merely being set, as VTE announces itself.

term.description: An exact TERM — Kitty is xterm-kitty.

encode.description: The bytes, as a template, for a terminal that does understand.

fallback.description: What to print when it does not — PRINCIPLES rule 6. '' is a legitimate answer, a window title having nothing to say in a log; absence is not, which is why this is required and may be ''.

capabilities.description: paratext capabilities by name — the OSC section of a plugin, read the way flagstaff reads `spinners`.

capabilityDocument.description: What paratext's `check()` accepts. Two shapes, and only one of them survives 1.0.

oneOf.description: The family shape: a plugin carrying its capabilities under `capabilities`.
Deprecated: one capability as the whole document, the shape paratext's schema had before this one absorbed it. Accepted for one minor release, removed at 1.0 — `check()` validates it and says so.
